core_obligations: Finiteness of the normalization (proof lines 3746-3762): reduce to an affine Noetherian domain A; let B be the integral closure of A in its fraction field and C the ring of global sections of the alteration; finiteness of cohomology on a proper scheme over an affine base makes C a finite A-module, normality of the source makes C a normal domain, and since B is contained in C it is finite over A because A is Noetherian.

A regular dense open (proof lines 3762-3773): by the definition of an alteration there is a nonempty open over which the morphism is finite, and after shrinking it may be taken flat by generic flatness, hence faithfully flat; descent of regularity along a faithfully flat morphism makes that open regular.
proof_roadmap: Use finiteness of cohomology and normality of the source to show the normalization is finite.
Find a nonempty open over which the alteration is finite and flat.
Descend regularity along that faithfully flat morphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a Noetherian integral scheme admitting an alteration from a regular scheme has finite normalization and a dense open which is regular (statement lines 3746-3752). The proof (proof lines 3753-3773) shows finiteness of the normalizations through the global sections of the alteration and finds a regular dense open by descending regularity along a generically finite flat morphism. H2: two complete independent arguments.
